To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel curriculum learning framework to guide the exploration of an RL agent in a large state-action space and we propose a novel neural network architecture to approximate the value function in such environments.

1) we propose a novel QWeb network architecture for Q-learning in Web navigation, 2) we propose guided RL methods for generating synthetic tasks, and 3) we propose a meta-learning framework to generate synthetic instruction following tasks.
1. We propose an approach to learn to follow natural language instructions by decomposing a complex task into a sequence of simpler tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: 1. How can we train RL agents to navigate the web with the help of demonstrations, when the number of possible instructions is large? 2. How can we generate synthetic tasks to train RL agents to learn from, when the number and the complexity of the tasks is large?

the following questions:
How can we decompose complex tasks into smaller sub-instructions to improve RL performance?
the problem of learning how to follow instructions from a large and unbounded space of possible instructions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed methods, which are based on a new QWeb network architecture, are able to successfully learn to navigate the web in environments that have large state and action space and sparse rewards.
we have proposed a novel approach for learning to navigate the web using deep reinforcement learning.
the proposed approach can learn to solve tasks in large state-action spaces with sparse rewards and can generalize to new tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel curriculum learning approach that can generate an unlimited amount of synthetic data for RL agent to learn from, and we have shown the effectiveness of our approach on large scale environments.
we propose a novel approach that enables an RL agent to learn from unbounded amount of data, and can be applied to many real-world problems with sparse rewards and large state and action space.
we are the first to train an agent that can successfully navigate the web with the help of a curriculum of sub-tasks and a novel QWeb architecture that can learn from the generated sub-tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by decomposing the task into smaller subtasks, an agent can learn to navigate the Web more effectively.

guided RL agents can be successfully trained to learn from unbounded amount of synthetic experience, and that they can be used to learn in environments where the number of possible instructions is too large for a human expert.

by decomposing the instruction following task and learning from a curriculum of sub-tasks, we can significantly improve the performance of RL agent in environments with large number of actions and states.
